title: What Drives Google Maps Visibility for Restaurants and Hotels
seoTitle: Google Maps Visibility for Restaurants and Hotels
seoDescription: How relevance, distance and prominence work for restaurants and hotels in Google Maps, and what menus, amenities, photos, reviews and booking links do.
excerpt: You cannot move your building, so Maps visibility comes down to matching what guests search for and showing Google that people know and like you.
imageAlt: Dimly lit restaurant dining room with set tables, wine glasses and wall sconces, and a staff member at the counter
imageIdea: Real photo of a restaurant dining room or hotel lobby at service, warm light, no visible logos or signage, not staged stock.
author: Michael Shad, Founder of The SocialDM
bodyHtml:
Google says local results in Maps are based primarily on three things: relevance, distance and prominence. For a restaurant or hotel, you cannot move your building, so the work is making your profile clearly match what guests search for and giving Google real evidence that people know and like you, through menus, amenities, photos, reviews and working booking links.

Everything below is grounded in what Google publishes. Where Google is silent, I say so.

What does Google say decides who shows up in Maps?

Relevance, distance and prominence. Google defines relevance as how well a Business Profile matches what someone is searching for, distance as how far each result is from the location in the search, and prominence as how well known a business is.

All three come from Google's page on how to improve your local ranking. The same page makes a point I find useful with owners: a business farther away can rank higher if Google judges it more likely to have what the searcher wants. Distance matters, but it is not the whole answer. The page also says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking.

How do relevance, distance and prominence apply to a restaurant or hotel?

Relevance is about your category, menu, amenities and description matching the search. Distance is mostly fixed. Prominence comes from reviews, ratings and how known you are, online and off.

FactorWhat it means for youWhat you can do
RelevanceDoes your profile say you have what the guest typed, like "patio," "gluten free" or "pet friendly hotel"?Choose an accurate primary category, fill in attributes and amenities, add a full menu or room details
DistanceHow close you are to the place the guest named or is standingKeep the address and pin exact; you cannot change where you are
ProminenceHow well known and well reviewed you areEarn steady reviews, reply to them, and give people real reasons to write and post about you

Why do menus matter so much for restaurants in Maps?

Menus are where guests and Google see what you actually serve, which drives how well you match searches for a dish, cuisine or dietary need. Google lets restaurants build a menu inside the Business Profile, upload menu photos or link to a menu on their website.

Google's help page on adding a menu covers all three options and asks owners to check a generated menu for accuracy before publishing. Google does not list menus as a ranking factor, so I would not oversell them. But a guest searching for birria tacos or a vegan brunch is trying to match on exactly what a menu contains. I want the menu in the profile, a text version on the website, and both updated the same day prices or dishes change. An out of date menu is an easy way to leave a guest feeling misled when they arrive.

What should a hotel fill in on its Google profile?

The category, accurate contact details, check in and check out times, and the full list of amenities, such as pool, parking, pets, breakfast and accessibility. Google summarizes hotel amenities for Search and Maps, and a verified owner can correct them.

Google's hotel Business Profile guide explains that the hotel's profile must be claimed and verified to edit all amenities, and that you edit them through the hotel details section. Check them yourself rather than trusting what was imported. A wrong "free parking" or a missing "pet friendly" is a relevance problem and a guest experience problem at the same time.

Do photos help a restaurant or hotel rank in Maps?

Google does not list photos as a ranking factor, but it does encourage businesses to add them, and they shape whether a guest picks you from the list. Google's photo tips page says your business must be verified for your photos to show, and recommends at least three interior and three exterior photos.

For restaurants I want the dining room at service, the patio, the bar and the dishes people order most. For hotels, every room type, the lobby, the pool and the view people will actually get. Story led content from your social channels often makes better profile photos than a staged shoot, because it shows the place as guests will find it.

How do reviews affect Maps visibility for hospitality businesses?

Google says review count and review score factor into local ranking, and that more reviews and positive ratings can improve it. Reviews are also the text guests read most closely before they book or reserve.

What I recommend:

  1. Ask for reviews in person, at the end of a good stay or meal, with a short link or QR code.
  2. Never offer anything in exchange for a review, and never ask only the happy guests to review on Google while steering the others elsewhere.
  3. Reply with something specific to what the guest said, and keep complaints calm and short.
  4. Read reviews for patterns. If several mention slow check in or a noisy room, that is an operations fix before it is a marketing fix.

Should you add booking and reservation links?

Yes. A working link from your profile to book a room or reserve a table removes a step for the guest. Restaurants can add a reservation link to the profile or use a reservation provider that connects with Google. Hotels can take part in Google's free booking links.

Google's page on hotel free booking links says partners pay no fee for them and that bids have no impact on how they rank. Ask your booking engine or channel manager whether your property is connected, and check that the rates shown match what your site charges. I would not claim these links improve your Maps rank, since Google does not say that. They do make it easier for a guest who found you to book you.

Google Maps is one part of the search and Google Business Profile work on our hospitality marketing page, where it sits alongside story led social and AI readiness.

Questions we hear

What are Google's three local ranking factors?

Google says local results are based primarily on relevance, distance and prominence. Relevance is how well your profile matches the search, distance is how far you are from the searched location, and prominence is how well known you are.

Can a restaurant or hotel pay to rank higher in Google Maps?

No. Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking.

Do hotel free booking links cost anything?

Google says hotel partners pay no fee for free booking links and that bids do not affect how they rank. Participation runs through Google Hotel Center, often set up by your booking engine or connectivity partner.

Does adding a menu help a restaurant show up in Maps?

Google does not list menus as a ranking factor. A complete, accurate menu does help your profile match dish and cuisine searches, and it helps guests choose you once they find you.

Why does a restaurant farther away outrank us?

Google says a business farther from the searcher can rank higher if its systems judge it more likely to have what the person wants. That usually points to relevance or prominence, not distance.

sources.claim: Local results based primarily on relevance, distance and prominence, with definitions; farther business can rank higher; review count and score factor in; more reviews and positive ratings can improve ranking; no way to pay for better local ranking
Restaurants can build a menu in the profile, upload menu photos or add a menu link; review generated menu for accuracy
Google summarizes hotel amenities for Search and Maps; profile must be claimed and verified to edit all amenities via Hotel details
Business must be verified for photos to show; add at least three interior and three exterior photos
Hotel free booking links: no fee for partners; bids have no impact on ranking

takeaways: Google says local results in Maps are based primarily on relevance, distance and prominence.
A restaurant or hotel farther from the searcher can still outrank a closer one if Google judges it a better match.
Complete menus, hotel amenities and real photos help your profile match what guests search for, even though Google does not list them as ranking factors.
Google says more reviews and positive ratings can improve local ranking, and nobody can pay for a better organic position.
